questions.prompt: What are the two major components of the .NET Framework?
options: The Just-in-Time compiler and the C# compiler
The Common Language Runtime (CLR) and the .NET Framework Class Library
Visual Studio and the NuGet package manager
MSIL and the Windows operating system
questions.explanation: The note names the Common Language Runtime and the .NET Framework Class Library as the two major components of the .NET Framework.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a job of the Base Class Library (BCL) rather than of the CLR?
options: Managing threads while the application runs
Providing APIs for reading and writing files and connecting to databases
Converting IL code into machine code
questions.explanation: The BCL provides types and APIs for common functionality such as strings, dates, files and databases. Garbage collection, thread management and running code are services of the CLR, the execution engine.

questions.prompt: Put the steps from source code to running program in order.
steps: Write the source code in C#, F# or VB
Compile the source code into intermediate language (IL / MSIL / CIL)
Store the compiled code in an assembly with a .dll or .exe extension
When the application runs, the CLR takes the assembly
The JIT compiler converts the IL into machine code for the computer's architecture
questions.explanation: Source code is compiled to IL and stored in an assembly; at run time the CLR uses the Just-in-Time compiler to turn that IL into machine code for the specific architecture.

questions.prompt: Which statement matches the note's comparison of .NET Core and the .NET Framework?
options: .NET Core is cross-platform (Windows, Mac OS X, Linux), while the .NET Framework was designed for Windows
.NET Core runs only on Windows, while the .NET Framework is cross-platform
Both run only on Windows, but .NET Core is open source
Both are cross-platform, but only the .NET Framework is free
questions.explanation: The note describes .NET Core as a free, open-source, cross-platform framework for Windows, Mac OS X and Linux, and the .NET Framework as a platform for building and running Windows applications.
